walks.title: Work a component where it is

steps.do: Open System. Choose Mission Computing Subsystem in the Subsystem filter, then click Mission Computer.
steps.see: The list narrows to its 3 components; hovering a row shows an eye for its preview; the click opens Mission Computer's page.
steps.was: Composition tree, then a preview, then a read-only Element page with the menu gone.

steps.do: Software & firmware → Add item: Firmware, MC-FW, 5.0. Then click the row and change the version.
steps.see: The row is there, the tab counts 5, System's row reads +2; the edit is kept.
steps.was: Rows were text; nothing could be added.

steps.do: Controls → Add controls, tick two, Add 2 controls.
steps.see: Both rows appear and the count follows; every control placed here is listed, with why.
steps.was: 12 of 98 codes shown; 'Open in Controls' opened all 560 unfiltered.

steps.do: Click one of them. On the control's page, write its implementation for Mission Computer; go Back.
steps.see: The control's page leads with Mission Computer; back on the tab the row reads Written.
steps.was: One narrative for the whole system, edited seven clicks away in the SSP.

steps.do: Requirements → Add requirement → Create requirement; choose that control.
steps.see: The new requirement is in the tab, mapped to the control; its row opens its page, which lists Mission Computer.
steps.was: 'Open in Requirements' left for the register.

steps.do: Overview → Take version 2, write the review comment.
steps.see: Still on Mission Computer, now version 2.
steps.was: A banner said 'Take it on Host & providers'.

steps.see: One table: the nine outside connections with ports and agreement, the host's interfaces, and the new one, Inside.

open: Pass 2: requirement and finding pages opened from a component do not carry the component in their breadcrumb (the control's page does); Back and the component's name on the page are the way back.

Pass 2: in a build without lanes C and D the stand-in previews k3s-ctl and k3s-req have no page, so those rows still open a preview on click; the whole build has no such row (asserted on 27 routes). walk.lane.mjs predates pass 2.
Pass 2: findings on a component are lane E's list on the whole build (Mission Computer 54, system 140; the lane alone derived 14 and 62).
Still printing the old count or another placement list (for the lead to point at fact componentCounts / controlsOf / requirementsOf / componentsOf):

1. PA.v7p.EBY itself (ctl, req, o, e, i, r; Mission Computer 98, 102, 358, 257, 7, 10) and its copies PA.SCTMD.els and mod-system.js SD.els. With V3 on, the only pages that printed ctl and req were Composition (tree, List) and the Element preview and page, all folded here; they still show in Compare with v2 and with V3 off.

2. Posture (route posture, which the shell now sends to controls; previews v7a-pel, sys-pel, v7a-pcell): component by family in objectives from mod-v7-analysis (Mission Computer 358 mapped, 257 with evidence, 7 issues, 10 risks), not from placements. Lane C's coverage view should count from controlsOf.

3. The workbook (sctm): SCTM sheet's 'Allocated to' is the components of the requirements that map the control (always a subset of componentsOf(control)), 'Responsible element' the first unit its narrative names; the Requirements sheet's 'Allocated to' is PA.SCTMD.reqs' els. Neither sees a control placed or a requirement allocated on a component, and both say element.

4. The SSP editor (ssp): section 5 'System tree, 27 elements' and section 8 'Hardware and software inventory, 20 elements' are fixed tables (no control counts): a component, firmware item, connection or port added here does not reach sections 5, 7, 8, 9.

5. The Requirements register (requirements, requirements-chain): 640 in its tab and pager against 115 requirement records held (42 allocated to a component); its 'Allocated to' column reads its own rows, not S's allocations.

6. Findings › By asset (findings-assets): issues and CVEs by its own rule (Mission Computer 1 issue, 1 CVE) against the component's Findings 14 (operational issues through its requirements, assessment findings short of satisfied on its controls, the SBOM's CVE).

The builds carry no charset line: Chromium sometimes reads out/*.html as Latin-1 (mojibake in ›, ·, ⌄; seen on prototype.html and once on v3r-S.html). meta.html needs <meta charset="utf-8">; S's scripts read a copy with a byte-order mark.

Ports are read by parsing the old ppsm page (12 services), the SBOM from the old element preview, the flight test instrumentation names from v2h-ext previews: those records are private to their modules (asks.json).
SSP section 5: the Boundary view's edit writes PA.SSP.sec('s5').text; text typed in the SSP editor (its private ST.secHTML) does not come back.
Host and provider interfaces (1553B, 1760, power, antennas, facility) are now connection records that 'ride on the provider's authorization': a modelling choice, no agreement asked.
Hardware rows derive the asset tag from the code scheme (AST-1090NN for CN-1091NN).

A created program: placements start empty; Add controls offers WS-X90's control list unless lane C's control fact says inBaseline false. Its host's responsibilities cannot be changed (v2host keeps them for WS-X90 only).
hosts opens System's list, not a provider; the Library components table is gone (only Mission Computer has a version to take).
composition-config's Submit Block 1.1 for approval and inventory-scans have no home in this lane.
The primary of a side panel is drawn as a secondary by v2's visual layer (one primary a screen).
Found by the re-walk, not fixed: a component's Software & firmware tab lists the unit itself as a Hardware row, and Add software or firmware offers Hardware as a kind.

one_number.truth: What stands on a component is the list this lane draws row by row. Controls: where a requirement allocated there maps the control, or the control's SSP implementation names the component, or the reader placed it; each row says which (Mapped by REQ-001, Named in its implementation, Placed here). Requirements: the requirement records held (PA.SCTMD.reqs, 115) allocated there, plus what the reader allocates or creates. A subsystem pools what is inside it.
one_number.read_it: PA.v3.fact('componentCounts', code) → { controls, requirements, findings, items, connections, components }; lists: controlsOf, requirementsOf, componentsOf(control). Every place lane S draws reads these (System's row, the component's tabs, its Overview, the Boundary, the component's panel on other pages): asserted in the walk.
one_number.numbers: Mission Computer: 74 controls, 13 requirements, 14 findings (was 98 and 102, PA.v7p.EBY's ctl and req, with 12 codes and 6 titles behind them). System: 543 controls, 42 requirements (was 547 and 640).

pass2.navigation_2: Nothing of S read #rail. System stays marked on every page of the lane, the connection's page included (asserted).
pass2.no_vertical_tabs: System's rail is gone, not turned into a dropdown: its kinds are the page's four tabs (Components 27, Host and providers 3, Connected systems 8, Connections 18), each with its own primary; Subsystem is a filter beside the search (K.toolbar filter, options with counts). A component's Controls tab: Family is a filter beside the search. Connections had no rail. K.rail and K.split are no longer called by this lane.
pass2.rows_and_eyes: Component rows (System, a subsystem's Components, a connection's 'Components it joins') go to the component's page and carry peek k3s-comp. A connection row goes to connection--<id>; the page is given crumbs System › Connections › name, a line From ↔ To · interface, ports with a Service column and Add port (header and section), the agreement with Link/Change agreement and No agreement needed, controls it bears on, and the components it joins. On a component, a control row goes to control--<code>@<component> (lane C), a requirement row to requirement--<id> (lane D), a finding row to finding--<id> (lane E); each lands right. Row buttons (Remove, Change) act alone. The bubble has one rule: a click goes to the record's page (a box to its component, a line and an inside-connection chip to the connection's page). After Add connection the reader stays on the tab; the toast offers Open connection. rec--v8b-ic--<id> opens the connection's page.
pass2.seam_cve: New fact cveFixed(cve, componentCode): true once the component (or one inside it) runs a version that fixes the CVE. Lane E reads it on the final build: after Take version 2 the CVE leaves Mission Computer's findings (asserted). The walk still asserts the step either way: with E reading it, without E, and prints a note if E is present and does not.
pass2.late_additions: Exports go through K.save (the kit's save: the viewer's prompt in the published page, a download from disk, a copy dialog otherwise). New fact items(componentCode) → { software, firmware, hardware } for lane D's SSP section 8; allocations stay [component, requirement] pairs under sys.alloc and sys.unalloc.
